q.t: A flagpole stands up straight. What kind of line does it make?
q.e: It goes straight up and down, like a person standing tall.

q.t: The top edge of a table goes straight from left to right. What kind of line is it?
q.e: It lies flat from side to side, like a person sleeping.

q.t: A ladder leaning against a wall makes a:
q.e: It is straight but tilted — neither straight up nor flat.

q.t: A rainbow makes a:
q.e: A rainbow bends like an arch, so it is curved.

q.t: Standing, sleeping and slanting lines are all:
q.e: They only point in different directions; none of them bends.

q.t: You lie flat on your back on the floor for a yoga pose. Your body makes a:
q.e: Lying flat means lying side to side, like a sleeping line.

q.t: You hold a thread tight between your two hands. It makes a:
q.e: Pulled tight, the thread cannot bend, so it is straight.

q.t: Now you bring your hands closer, and the thread hangs down. It makes a:
q.e: The loose thread sags and bends, so it is curved.

q.t: Which letter is made only of straight lines?
q.e: L is one standing line and one sleeping line; O, C and S bend.

q.t: Which letter has a curved line?
q.e: C bends round; T, L and E use only straight lines.

q.t: How many straight lines make the capital letter T?
q.e: One sleeping line on top and one standing line down the middle.

q.t: How many standing (vertical) lines are in the capital letter H?
q.e: H has a standing line on the left and one on the right.

q.t: How many sleeping (horizontal) lines are in the capital letter H?
q.e: Only the middle bar of H lies flat.

q.t: The capital letter V is made of:
q.e: Both arms of V are tilted and meet at the bottom.

q.t: The capital letter D is made of:
o: One standing line and one curved line
q.e: D has a straight back and a round front.

q.t: The side edge of a closed door makes a:
q.e: The door’s side edge goes straight up from the floor.

q.t: A slide in the park goes down at a tilt. It makes a:
q.e: It is tilted, not straight up and not flat — slanting.

q.t: Where the sea meets the sky looks like a:
q.e: It stretches flat from side to side.

q.t: Which shape has no straight lines?
q.e: A circle is one curved line all the way round.

q.t: At 6 o’clock the clock hands point straight up and straight down. Together they make a:
q.e: One hand points to 12 (up) and one to 6 (down), forming one straight up-down line.

q.t: How many straight lines make a triangle?
q.e: A triangle has 3 straight sides.

q.t: How many sleeping (horizontal) lines are in the capital letter E?
q.e: E has a top bar, a middle bar and a bottom bar.

q.t: How many straight lines in all make the capital letter E?
q.e: 1 standing line on the left and 3 sleeping lines: 1 + 3 = 4.

q.t: The capital letter A is made of:
o: Two slanting lines and one sleeping line
q.e: Two tilted sides meet at the top, and a flat bar joins them.

q.t: How many slanting lines make the capital letter W?
q.e: W goes down, up, down, up — 4 tilted strokes.

q.t: The capital letter M has two standing sides. How many slanting lines does it have?
q.e: The two middle strokes of M are tilted and meet in a point.

q.t: The capital letter N is made of:
o: Two standing lines and one slanting line
q.e: N has a standing line on each side and one tilted line joining them.

q.t: Which letter uses both a straight line and a curved line?
q.e: P has a straight back and a curved loop; O is all curved; T and X are all straight.

q.t: You fold a paper in half and open it. What does the fold (crease) look like?
q.e: Pressing a fold flat makes a sharp, straight crease.

q.t: A tree has a trunk going straight up and branches going up to the sides. What lines do you see?
q.e: The trunk stands up straight, and the branches tilt outwards.

q.t: A square has 2 sleeping lines (top and bottom). A triangle with a flat base has 1 sleeping line. How many sleeping lines in all?
q.e: Square 2 + triangle 1 = 3.

q.t: How many straight lines are there in the capital letters T, L and H together?
q.e: T has 2, L has 2, H has 3: 2 + 2 + 3 = 7.

q.t: In the word HI (written as simple capital letters, with I as one standing line), how many standing lines are there?
q.e: H has 2 standing lines and I has 1: 2 + 1 = 3.

q.t: How many slanting lines are in the capital letters X and V together?
q.e: X has 2 crossing slanting lines and V has 2: 2 + 2 = 4.

q.t: Which word is written with straight lines only?
q.e: T, I and E are all straight. C, U, B, O and S each have a curve.

q.t: Which capital letter is made of just one curved line, with no straight line?
q.e: D, P and B each have a straight back; O is one curved line all round.

q.t: You draw a house: a square wall with a triangle roof sitting on top (they share the line between them). How many slanting lines are there?
q.e: Only the two sides of the roof are tilted; the wall lines stand or lie flat.

q.t: In the same house (a square wall with a triangle roof sharing one line), how many straight lines are there in all?
q.e: Square 4 + triangle 3 = 7, but the shared line is counted twice, so 7 − 1 = 6.

q.t: Which yoga pose shows a sleeping (horizontal) line?
o: Bending your back into a curve
Leaning to one side with arms tilted
q.e: Lying flat makes the body go side to side, like a sleeping line.

q.t: A zigzag line is made of:
q.e: A zigzag goes up-tilted, down-tilted, up-tilted … each piece is a straight slanting line.
